record.paper_title: The Lieb-Thirring inequalities: recent results and open problems
record.context_brief: Removing the 1−ε loss in the improved bound
record.original_question: In the improved orthonormal Lieb-Thirring inequality with a semiclassical main term and an additional gradient-error term, can one remove the prefactor 1−ε in front of the semiclassical term while still keeping a finite constant in front of the gradient correction?

evidence.quote: It is an interesting open question whether the inequality holds without the factor 1 − ε in front of the first term and with a finite constant in front of the gradient term.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $d\ge 1$ and let $(u_j)_{j=1}^N$ be an orthonormal family in $L^2(\mathbb{R}^d)$. Define the one-particle density
$$\rho(x)=\sum_{j=1}^N |u_j(x)|^2,\qquad x\in\mathbb{R}^d,$$
and the kinetic energy
$$T[(u_j)]=\sum_{j=1}^N \int_{\mathbb{R}^d}|\nabla u_j(x)|^2\,dx.$$
Let $K_{\rm cl}(d)=\frac{d}{d+2}\bigl(4\pi^2\bigr)\bigl(\Gamma(d/2+1)\bigr)^{-2/d}$ be the semiclassical Lieb–Thirring constant, so that
$$\int_{\mathbb{R}^d}\rho(x)^{1+2/d}\,dx$$
is the natural Thomas–Fermi-type density functional appearing in the semiclassical kinetic energy.

It is known that for every $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$ there exists a constant $C(d,\varepsilon)<\infty$ such that, for every orthonormal family as above,
$$T[(u_j)]\;\ge\;(1-\varepsilon)\,K_{\rm cl}(d)\int_{\mathbb{R}^d}\rho(x)^{1+2/d}\,dx\;-\;C(d,\varepsilon)\int_{\mathbb{R}^d}\bigl|\nabla\sqrt{\rho(x)}\bigr|^2\,dx.$$

Question: Does there exist a finite constant $C(d)<\infty$ such that, for every orthonormal family $(u_j)_{j=1}^N$ in $L^2(\mathbb{R}^d)$,
$$T[(u_j)]\;\ge\;K_{\rm cl}(d)\int_{\mathbb{R}^d}\rho(x)^{1+2/d}\,dx\;-\;C(d)\int_{\mathbb{R}^d}\bigl|\nabla\sqrt{\rho(x)}\bigr|^2\,dx\,?$$
That is, can the prefactor $(1-\varepsilon)$ in front of the semiclassical term be replaced by $1$ while keeping a finite constant in front of the gradient correction term?
artifact.status_search_result: The improved orthonormal Lieb–Thirring inequality with semiclassical constant $(1-\varepsilon)K_{\rm cl}(d)$ and a gradient correction term is established in the literature (Nam, J. Funct. Anal. 2018; with simplified proofs in subsequent works such as the 2023 "simple approach" paper). Whether one can take $\varepsilon=0$ while keeping a finite gradient-term constant is consistently described as an open question; recent surveys on the state of the Lieb–Thirring inequalities (2022–2023) still list this as an open problem, with no published resolution found.

status_evidence.title: Lieb-Thirring inequality with semiclassical constant and gradient error term
status_evidence.snippet: Improved bound with semiclassical constant (1-epsilon) and a gradient error term of lower order.
status_evidence.claim: Establishes the bound with a (1-epsilon) prefactor and gradient correction, motivating the question of removing epsilon.

status_evidence.title: A simple approach to Lieb–Thirring type inequalities
status_evidence.snippet: We present a stronger version of this inequality, with a much simplified proof.
status_evidence.claim: Provides simplified/strengthened versions but still operates within the (1-epsilon) framework.

status_evidence.title: The state of the Lieb–Thirring inequality
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of recent results and open problems on Lieb-Thirring inequalities.
status_evidence.claim: Recent survey discussing open problems around the semiclassical constant in such inequalities.
